objects.definition:
enum libusb_class_code {
	LIBUSB_CLASS_PER_INTERFACE = 0x00,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_AUDIO = 0x01,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_COMM = 0x02,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_HID = 0x03,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_PHYSICAL = 0x05,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_IMAGE = 0x06,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_PTP = 0x06,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_PRINTER = 0x07,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_MASS_STORAGE = 0x08,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_HUB = 0x09,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_DATA = 0x0a,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_SMART_CARD = 0x0b,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_CONTENT_SECURITY = 0x0d,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_VIDEO = 0x0e,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_PERSONAL_HEALTHCARE = 0x0f,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_DIAGNOSTIC_DEVICE = 0xdc,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_WIRELESS = 0xe0,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_MISCELLANEOUS = 0xef,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_APPLICATION = 0xfe,
	LIBUSB_CLASS_VENDOR_SPEC = 0xff
};
objects.description: USB device/interface class codes used in descriptors (bDeviceClass, bInterfaceClass).

objects.definition:
enum libusb_descriptor_type {
	LIBUSB_DT_DEVICE = 0x01,
	LIBUSB_DT_CONFIG = 0x02,
	LIBUSB_DT_STRING = 0x03,
	LIBUSB_DT_INTERFACE = 0x04,
	LIBUSB_DT_ENDPOINT = 0x05,
	LIBUSB_DT_INTERFACE_ASSOCIATION = 0x0b,
	LIBUSB_DT_BOS = 0x0f,
	LIBUSB_DT_DEVICE_CAPABILITY = 0x10,
	LIBUSB_DT_HID = 0x21,
	LIBUSB_DT_REPORT = 0x22,
	LIBUSB_DT_PHYSICAL = 0x23,
	LIBUSB_DT_HUB = 0x29,
	LIBUSB_DT_SUPERSPEED_HUB = 0x2a,
	LIBUSB_DT_SS_ENDPOINT_COMPANION = 0x30
};
objects.description: USB standard descriptor type codes.
Bit 7 values for endpoint direction used in bEndpointAddress.
Transfer type bits (0:1) for endpoint bmAttributes.

objects.definition:
enum libusb_standard_request {
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_GET_STATUS = 0x00,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_CLEAR_FEATURE = 0x01,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_SET_FEATURE = 0x03,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_SET_ADDRESS = 0x05,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_GET_DESCRIPTOR = 0x06,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_SET_DESCRIPTOR = 0x07,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_GET_CONFIGURATION = 0x08,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_SET_CONFIGURATION = 0x09,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_GET_INTERFACE = 0x0a,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_SET_INTERFACE = 0x0b,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_SYNCH_FRAME = 0x0c,
	LIBUSB_REQUEST_SET_SEL = 0x30,
	LIBUSB_SET_ISOCH_DELAY = 0x31
};
objects.description: USB standard control request codes (bRequest).
Request type bits (5:6) for bmRequestType in control transfers.
Recipient field values (0:4) for bmRequestType in control transfers.
Isochronous synchronization type values for bmAttributes (bits 2:3).
Isochronous usage type values for bmAttributes (bits 4:5).
Bitfield indicating device supported speeds in BOS capabilities.
USB 2.0 Extension descriptor bmAttributes bits (LPM support).
SuperSpeed USB Device Capability bmAttributes bits (LTM support).
BOS device capability types.
Standard USB device descriptor structure.
Standard USB endpoint descriptor with optional extra descriptors.
USB Interface Association Descriptor (IAD) structure.
Container holding an array of IAD descriptors returned by helper APIs.
Standard USB interface descriptor, including endpoints array.
Collection of alternate settings for a USB interface.
Standard USB configuration descriptor with interfaces and extra data.
SuperSpeed endpoint companion descriptor.
Generic BOS device capability descriptor header with flexible payload.
BOS (Binary Object Store) descriptor containing capability descriptors.
USB 2.0 Extension BOS capability descriptor.
SuperSpeed USB Device Capability descriptor.
SS+ sublink attribute: symmetric or asymmetric.
SS+ sublink attribute: direction RX or TX.
SS+ sublink attribute exponent units (bps, Kbps, Mbps, Gbps).
SS+ sublink attribute protocol (SS or SS+).
Parsed view of a SuperSpeedPlus Sublink Speed Attribute entry.
SuperSpeedPlus USB Device Capability descriptor with sublink attributes array.
Container ID BOS capability containing a UUID.
Platform capability BOS descriptor with vendor-defined payload.
Packed USB control transfer setup packet header (8 bytes).
Holds libusb runtime version information.

objects.definition: typedef struct libusb_context libusb_context;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a libusb session context. Created with libusb_init/libusb_init_context and freed by libusb_exit.

objects.definition: typedef struct libusb_device libusb_device;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a discovered USB device. Ref-counted via libusb_ref_device/libusb_unref_device and obtained from libusb_get_device_list or libusb_get_device.

objects.definition: typedef struct libusb_device_handle libusb_device_handle;
objects.description: Opaque handle for an open USB device used for I/O. Created by libusb_open/libusb_open_device_with_vid_pid/libusb_wrap_sys_device and closed by libusb_close.
Enumerates the current operating speed of a USB device.

objects.definition:
enum libusb_error {
	LIBUSB_SUCCESS = 0,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_IO = -1,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_INVALID_PARAM = -2,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS = -3,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_NO_DEVICE = -4,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_NOT_FOUND = -5,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_BUSY = -6,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_TIMEOUT = -7,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_OVERFLOW = -8,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_PIPE = -9,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_INTERRUPTED = -10,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_NO_MEM = -11,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED = -12,
	LIBUSB_ERROR_OTHER = -99
};
objects.description: Libusb function return error codes (negative for errors).
Transfer type values used in libusb_transfer.type.
Result status of an asynchronous transfer.
Flags modifying libusb_transfer behavior.
Per-isochronous-packet descriptor for isochronous transfers.
Generic async USB transfer descriptor used for all transfer types.
Feature flags indicating capabilities supported by the loaded libusb backend.
Log verbosity levels for libusb internal logging.
Controls whether a log callback applies globally or per-context.
Options for libusb_set_option and libusb_init_context.
Indices for retrieving device string descriptors via helper API.

objects.definition:
typedef void (LIBUSB_CALL *libusb_log_cb)(libusb_context *ctx,
	enum libusb_log_level level, const char *str);
objects.description: Function pointer type for log callbacks used with libusb_set_log_cb or LIBUSB_OPTION_LOG_CB.
Name/value option item used to initialize a context via libusb_init_context.
Represents a pollable file descriptor and events for integration with event loops.

objects.definition:
typedef void (LIBUSB_CALL *libusb_pollfd_added_cb)(int fd, short events,
	void *user_data);
objects.description: Callback type notified when libusb adds a pollfd.

objects.definition: typedef void (LIBUSB_CALL *libusb_pollfd_removed_cb)(int fd, void *user_data);
objects.description: Callback type notified when libusb removes a pollfd.

objects.definition: typedef int libusb_hotplug_callback_handle;
objects.description: Opaque integer handle identifying a registered hotplug callback.
Bitmask values for hotplug events used when registering callbacks.
Flags modifying hotplug callback registration behavior.

objects.definition:
typedef int (LIBUSB_CALL *libusb_hotplug_callback_fn)(libusb_context *ctx,
	libusb_device *device, libusb_hotplug_event event, void *user_data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for hotplug notification callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef void (LIBUSB_CALL *libusb_transfer_cb_fn)(struct libusb_transfer *transfer);
objects.description: Function pointer type for asynchronous transfer completion callbacks.

functions.name: libusb_cpu_to_le16
functions.description: Convert a 16-bit host-endian value to little-endian. On little-endian hosts it returns x unchanged; on big-endian it swaps bytes.
requirements: x is any 16-bit value

functions.name: libusb_init
functions.description: Initialize a new libusb context or the default one if ctx is NULL. Call libusb_exit() when done.
requirements: ctx may be NULL to use the default context; otherwise must be a valid pointer to receive the context
Must be called before most other libusb functions (except version/error helpers)
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_init_context
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_init_context(libusb_context **ctx, const struct libusb_init_option options[], int num_options)
functions.description: Initialize a libusb context with explicit options (log level, backend use, etc.). Preferred when you need to configure options at init time.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to receive the created context
options may be NULL or point to an array of libusb_init_option entries
num_options must be >= 0 and reflect the number of entries in options
Must call libusb_exit() to destroy the context
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_exit
functions.description: Deinitialize and free a libusb context created by libusb_init()/libusb_init_context(). For NULL, destroys the default context.
requirements: ctx may be NULL to refer to the default context
Do not use the context after calling this function
Should balance a prior successful libusb_init()/libusb_init_context()

functions.name: libusb_set_debug
functions.description: Set the logging verbosity for a context (deprecated in favor of libusb_set_option or libusb_set_log_cb via options).
requirements: ctx may be NULL to use the default context
level is a libusb_log_level integer
Has no effect if library compiled without logging or overridden by environment/compile options

functions.name: libusb_set_log_cb
functions.signature: void LIBUSB_CALL libusb_set_log_cb(libusb_context *ctx, libusb_log_cb cb, int mode)
functions.description: Install a log callback to receive libusb log messages globally (ctx==NULL) or for a specific context (ctx!=NULL). Mode selects GLOBAL or CONTEXT handling.
requirements: cb may be NULL to clear the callback
mode should be a bitwise OR of libusb_log_cb_mode values
Thread-safety: callback may be invoked from internal threads; keep it lightweight

functions.name: libusb_get_version
functions.description: Return a pointer to a static struct describing the runtime libusb version.
requirements: Returned pointer is owned by libusb and must not be freed or modified

functions.name: libusb_has_capability
functions.description: Check if the loaded libusb library supports a capability (e.g., hotplug, HID access).
requirements: capability must be one of libusb_capability values
Returns nonzero if supported, 0 otherwise

functions.name: libusb_error_name
functions.description: Return a constant string name for a libusb_error value.
requirements: error_code should be a value from enum libusb_error; unknown codes may return an implementation-defined string
Returned string must not be freed

functions.name: libusb_setlocale
functions.description: Set the locale used for human-readable error strings (affects libusb_strerror()).
requirements: locale is a C locale string (e.g., "C", "en_US") or NULL to reset, per implementation
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_strerror
functions.description: Return a human-readable (possibly localized) description string for a libusb_error code.
requirements: errcode should be a value from enum libusb_error; unknown codes may return a generic message
Returned string must not be freed

functions.name: libusb_get_device_list
functions.description: Enumerate currently connected USB devices and return an array of libusb_device pointers.
requirements: ctx may be NULL to use default context
list must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a NULL-terminated array
On success returns number of devices; on failure negative libusb_error
Call libusb_free_device_list() to free the list; may also unref devices

functions.name: libusb_free_device_list
functions.description: Free a device list returned by libusb_get_device_list(). Optionally unref each device.
requirements: list must be a list obtained from libusb_get_device_list() or NULL
If unref_devices is nonzero, each device in the list is unreferenced

functions.name: libusb_ref_device
functions.description: Increase the reference count of a libusb_device and return it.
requirements: dev must be a valid device pointer
Ensure each ref is eventually matched with libusb_unref_device()

functions.name: libusb_unref_device
functions.description: Decrease the reference count of a libusb_device; frees when it reaches zero.
requirements: dev must be a valid device pointer obtained from libusb or NULL
Do not use the device after its final unref

functions.name: libusb_get_device_string
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_device_string(libusb_device *dev, enum libusb_device_string_type string_type, char *data, int length)
functions.description: Fetch a device string (manufacturer, product, serial) in UTF-8 into a caller buffer.
requirements: dev must be a valid device
string_type must be one of libusb_device_string_type
data must be a writable buffer; length must be >= 0 and at least LIBUSB_DEVICE_STRING_BYTES_MAX to hold maximum
Returns number of bytes written or a negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_get_configuration
functions.description: Get the active configuration value for an open device handle.
requirements: dev must be an open device handle
config must be a valid pointer to receive the configuration number
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_get_device_descriptor
functions.description: Retrieve the standard device descriptor for a device.
requirements: dev must be a valid device
desc must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_get_active_config_descriptor
functions.description: Get the currently active configuration descriptor. The returned descriptor must be freed with libusb_free_config_descriptor().
requirements: dev must be a valid device
config must be a valid pointer to receive an allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Caller must free via libusb_free_config_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_get_config_descriptor
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_config_descriptor(libusb_device *dev, uint8_t config_index, struct libusb_config_descriptor **config)
functions.description: Get a configuration descriptor by index from a device. Must be freed with libusb_free_config_descriptor().
requirements: dev must be valid
config_index is a zero-based configuration index
config must be a valid pointer to receive allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_config_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_get_config_descriptor_by_value
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_config_descriptor_by_value(libusb_device *dev, uint8_t bConfigurationValue, struct libusb_config_descriptor **config)
functions.description: Get a configuration descriptor matching bConfigurationValue. Must be freed with libusb_free_config_descriptor().
requirements: dev must be valid
config must be a valid pointer to receive allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_config_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_free_config_descriptor
functions.description: Free a configuration descriptor allocated by a libusb_get_*_config_descriptor() call.
requirements: config must be a descriptor obtained from libusb_get_*_config_descriptor functions or NULL
Do not use the descriptor after freeing

functions.name: libusb_get_ss_endpoint_companion_descriptor
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_ss_endpoint_companion_descriptor(libusb_context *ctx, const struct libusb_endpoint_descriptor *endpoint, struct libusb_ss_endpoint_companion_descriptor **ep_comp)
functions.description: Parse and return the SuperSpeed Endpoint Companion descriptor for a given endpoint descriptor.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
endpoint must point to a valid endpoint descriptor
ep_comp must be a valid pointer to receive an allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_ss_endpoint_companion_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_free_ss_endpoint_companion_descriptor
functions.description: Free a SuperSpeed Endpoint Companion descriptor previously allocated by libusb_get_ss_endpoint_companion_descriptor().
requirements: ep_comp may be NULL or a pointer obtained from libusb_get_ss_endpoint_companion_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_get_bos_descriptor
functions.description: Retrieve the Binary Object Store (BOS) descriptor from an open device handle.
requirements: dev_handle must be an open device handle
bos must be a valid pointer to receive an allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_bos_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_free_bos_descriptor
functions.description: Free a BOS descriptor obtained by libusb_get_bos_descriptor().
requirements: bos may be NULL or a BOS descriptor returned by libusb_get_bos_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_get_usb_2_0_extension_descriptor
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_usb_2_0_extension_descriptor(libusb_context *ctx, struct libusb_bos_dev_capability_descriptor *dev_cap, struct libusb_usb_2_0_extension_descriptor **usb_2_0_extension)
functions.description: Parse a BOS device capability as a USB 2.0 Extension descriptor.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
dev_cap must be a BOS capability descriptor of type LIBUSB_BT_USB_2_0_EXTENSION
usb_2_0_extension must be a pointer to receive an allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_usb_2_0_extension_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_free_usb_2_0_extension_descriptor
functions.description: Free a USB 2.0 Extension descriptor allocated by libusb_get_usb_2_0_extension_descriptor().
requirements: usb_2_0_extension may be NULL or a pointer obtained from libusb_get_usb_2_0_extension_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_get_ss_usb_device_capability_descriptor
functions.description: Parse a BOS device capability as a SuperSpeed USB Device Capability descriptor.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
dev_cap must be a BOS capability descriptor of type LIBUSB_BT_SS_USB_DEVICE_CAPABILITY
ss_usb_device_cap must receive an allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_ss_usb_device_capability_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_free_ss_usb_device_capability_descriptor
functions.description: Free a SuperSpeed USB Device Capability descriptor allocated by libusb_get_ss_usb_device_capability_descriptor().
requirements: ss_usb_device_cap may be NULL or a pointer obtained from its matching get function

functions.name: libusb_get_ssplus_usb_device_capability_descriptor
functions.description: Parse a BOS device capability as a SuperSpeedPlus USB Device Capability descriptor.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
dev_cap must be a BOS capability descriptor of type LIBUSB_BT_SUPERSPEED_PLUS_CAPABILITY
ssplus_usb_device_cap must receive an allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_ssplus_usb_device_capability_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_free_ssplus_usb_device_capability_descriptor
functions.description: Free a SuperSpeedPlus USB Device Capability descriptor allocated by its matching get function.
requirements: ssplus_usb_device_cap may be NULL or a pointer obtained from libusb_get_ssplus_usb_device_capability_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_get_container_id_descriptor
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_container_id_descriptor(libusb_context *ctx, struct libusb_bos_dev_capability_descriptor *dev_cap, struct libusb_container_id_descriptor **container_id)
functions.description: Parse a BOS device capability as a Container ID descriptor.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
dev_cap must be a BOS capability descriptor of type LIBUSB_BT_CONTAINER_ID
container_id must receive an allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_container_id_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_free_container_id_descriptor
functions.description: Free a Container ID descriptor allocated by its matching get function.
requirements: container_id may be NULL or a pointer returned by libusb_get_container_id_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_get_platform_descriptor
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_platform_descriptor(libusb_context *ctx, struct libusb_bos_dev_capability_descriptor *dev_cap, struct libusb_platform_descriptor **platform_descriptor)
functions.description: Parse a BOS device capability as a Platform descriptor.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
dev_cap must be a BOS capability descriptor of type LIBUSB_BT_PLATFORM_DESCRIPTOR
platform_descriptor must receive an allocated descriptor
Returns 0 on success or a negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_platform_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_free_platform_descriptor
functions.description: Free a Platform descriptor allocated by libusb_get_platform_descriptor().
requirements: platform_descriptor may be NULL or a pointer returned by libusb_get_platform_descriptor()

functions.name: libusb_get_session_data
functions.description: Return a session-specific opaque value for the device (e.g., unique session ID).
requirements: dev must be valid
Return value format is implementation-defined

functions.name: libusb_get_bus_number
functions.description: Get the bus number a device is connected to.
requirements: dev must be valid

functions.name: libusb_get_port_number
functions.description: Get the device’s port number on its parent hub.
requirements: dev must be valid

functions.name: libusb_get_port_numbers
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_port_numbers(libusb_device *dev, uint8_t *port_numbers, int port_numbers_len)
functions.description: Get the hop port path from root hub to the device as a sequence of port numbers.
requirements: dev must be valid
port_numbers must point to a writable array
port_numbers_len must be >= 0 and large enough to hold the path
Returns number of entries filled or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_get_port_path
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_port_path(libusb_context *ctx, libusb_device *dev, uint8_t *path, uint8_t path_length)
functions.description: Deprecated. Use libusb_get_port_numbers(). Retrieves the device path as a sequence of port numbers.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
dev must be valid
path must point to a writable array; path_length is its capacity
Returns number of entries filled or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_get_parent
functions.description: Get the parent device in the topology, or NULL if root or unknown.
requirements: dev must be valid
Returned device may be NULL; if non-NULL, its ownership follows libusb rules (likely not ref-counted; consult implementation)

functions.name: libusb_get_device_address
functions.description: Get the device address on its bus.
requirements: dev must be valid

functions.name: libusb_get_device_speed
functions.description: Get device operating speed as a libusb_speed enum value.
requirements: dev must be valid
Returns a libusb_speed or LIBUSB_SPEED_UNKNOWN

functions.name: libusb_get_max_packet_size
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_max_packet_size(libusb_device *dev, unsigned char endpoint)
functions.description: Get the maximum packet size for the specified endpoint on a device (considering current altsetting).
requirements: dev must be valid
endpoint is the endpoint address (with direction bit as appropriate)
Returns positive size or a negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_get_max_iso_packet_size
functions.description: Get the maximum isochronous packet size for the specified endpoint.
requirements: dev must be valid
endpoint is the endpoint address
Returns positive size or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_get_max_alt_packet_size
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_get_max_alt_packet_size(libusb_device *dev, int interface_number, int alternate_setting, unsigned char endpoint)
functions.description: Get the maximum packet size for an endpoint in a specified interface alternate setting.
requirements: dev must be valid
interface_number and alternate_setting must be valid for the device
endpoint is the endpoint address
Returns positive size or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_get_interface_association_descriptors
functions.description: Retrieve all Interface Association Descriptors (IADs) for a configuration index. Must be freed with libusb_free_interface_association_descriptors().
requirements: dev must be valid
config_index is zero-based
iad_array must be a valid pointer to receive an allocated array
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_interface_association_descriptors()

functions.name: libusb_get_active_interface_association_descriptors
functions.description: Retrieve all IADs for the active configuration. Must be freed with libusb_free_interface_association_descriptors().
requirements: dev must be valid
iad_array must be a valid pointer to receive allocated data
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error
Free with libusb_free_interface_association_descriptors()

functions.name: libusb_free_interface_association_descriptors
functions.description: Free an IAD array allocated by libusb_get_*_interface_association_descriptors().
requirements: iad_array may be NULL or a pointer returned by the matching get functions

functions.name: libusb_wrap_sys_device
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_wrap_sys_device(libusb_context *ctx, intptr_t sys_dev, libusb_device_handle **dev_handle)
functions.description: Wrap an existing OS-specific device handle (file descriptor/handle) into a libusb_device_handle.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
sys_dev must be a valid OS device identifier for the backend
dev_handle must be a valid pointer to receive the opened handle
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_open
functions.description: Open a libusb_device to obtain a device handle for I/O.
requirements: dev must be valid
dev_handle must be a valid pointer to receive the handle
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error
Close with libusb_close()

functions.name: libusb_close
functions.description: Close a device handle previously opened by libusb_open() or libusb_wrap_sys_device().
requirements: dev_handle may be NULL or a valid open handle
After closing, the handle must not be used

functions.name: libusb_get_device
functions.description: Get the libusb_device associated with an open device handle.
requirements: dev_handle must be a valid open handle
Returned device is owned by libusb; follow reference rules per implementation

functions.name: libusb_set_configuration
functions.description: Set the active configuration for a device by value.
requirements: dev_handle must be open
configuration is the desired bConfigurationValue
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_claim_interface
functions.description: Claim an interface before performing I/O on its endpoints.
requirements: dev_handle must be open
interface_number must exist on the device
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error
Must be released with libusb_release_interface()

functions.name: libusb_release_interface
functions.description: Release a previously claimed interface.
requirements: dev_handle must be open
interface_number must have been successfully claimed
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_open_device_with_vid_pid
functions.signature: libusb_device_handle * LIBUSB_CALL libusb_open_device_with_vid_pid(libusb_context *ctx, uint16_t vendor_id, uint16_t product_id)
functions.description: Open the first device matching a given VID/PID and return a device handle, or NULL on failure.
requirements: ctx may be NULL
vendor_id and product_id are the USB IDs to match
Returns NULL on failure or if not found
Close the returned handle with libusb_close()

functions.name: libusb_set_interface_alt_setting
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_set_interface_alt_setting(libusb_device_handle *dev_handle, int interface_number, int alternate_setting)
functions.description: Activate an alternate setting for an interface.
requirements: dev_handle must be open
interface_number and alternate_setting must be valid
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_clear_halt
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_clear_halt(libusb_device_handle *dev_handle, unsigned char endpoint)
functions.description: Clear a halt/stall condition on an endpoint (RESET_ENDPOINT feature).
requirements: dev_handle must be open
endpoint is the endpoint address
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error

functions.name: libusb_reset_device
functions.description: Perform a USB port reset on the device.
requirements: dev_handle must be open
Returns 0 on success or negative libusb_error
May change device state; interfaces may need to be re-claimed

functions.name: libusb_alloc_streams
functions.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_alloc_streams(libusb_device_handle *dev_handle, uint32_t num_streams, unsigned char *endpoints, int num_endpoints)
functions.description: Allocate USB 3.0 bulk streams for the specified endpoints.

generators.generator:
import random
import string

# Generator for locale-like strings suitable for libusb_setlocale fuzzing stub
# Returns bytes (UTF-8) with a NUL-terminated C string expectation handled by fuzzer

LANG_CODES = [
    # Common ISO 639-1 language codes
    'en','de','fr','es','it','pt','ru','zh','ja','ko','ar','nl','sv','no','da','fi','pl','cs','tr','el','he','hi','id','ms','vi','th','uk','ro','hu','sk','bg','hr','sr','sl','et','lv','lt','is','ga','mt','cy','eu','ca']
REGIONS = [
    # Common ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 regions
    'US','GB','DE','FR','ES','IT','PT','RU','CN','TW','HK','JP','KR','BR','MX','CA','AU','NZ','IN','ZA','SE','NO','DK','FI','PL','CZ','TR','GR','IL','IE','RO','HU','SK','BG','HR','RS','SI','EE','LV','LT']
CODESETS = [
    'UTF-8','utf8','ISO8859-1','ISO8859-15','ISO-8859-1','CP1252','KOI8-R','GB18030','GB2312','Big5','Shift_JIS','EUC-JP','EUC-KR']
MODIFIERS = ['@euro','@calendar=gregorian','@collation=phonebook','@currency=EUR','@pinyin','@stroke']
# POSIX-style special names
SPECIALS = ['C','POSIX']

# Some typical vendor/OS variants
VENDOR_PREFIXES = ['','C.','en_US.','de_DE.','']

# Max size per stub: 32 chars
MAX_LEN = 32


def _rand_locale_parts(r: random.Random):
    parts = []
    # Sometimes use special names directly
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        parts.append(r.choice(SPECIALS))
        return ''.join(parts)

    # Language
    lang = r.choice(LANG_CODES)
    # Occasionally use 3-letter or mixed case variant
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        lang = (lang + r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase)).lower()
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        lang = lang.upper() if r.random() < 0.5 else lang.capitalize()

    locale = lang

    # Optional region
    if r.random() < 0.85:
        region = r.choice(REGIONS)
        # Occasionally lower case region to test leniency
        if r.random() < 0.1:
            region = region.lower()
        locale += '_' + region

    # Optional codeset
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        codeset = r.choice(CODESETS)
        # sometimes tweak separators or case
        if r.random() < 0.15:
            codeset = codeset.replace('-', '').replace('_', '')
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            codeset = codeset.lower()
        locale += '.' + codeset

    # Optional modifier (at-sign or key=value style already included in MODIFIERS)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        locale += r.choice(MODIFIERS)

    return locale


def _random_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Produce generic token-like ASCII strings that still look plausible
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-@.+"
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(r.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid starting with NUL-equivalent or dot/at that might be odd
    if s and s[0] in '.@':
        s = 'C' + s
    return s


def _make_candidate(r: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = r.random()
    if mode < 0.60:
        s = _rand_locale_parts(r)
    elif mode < 0.80:
        # Known specials and variants
        base = r.choice(SPECIALS)
        # sometimes append codeset or modifier
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            base += '.' + r.choice(CODESETS)
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            base += r.choice(MODIFIERS)
        s = base
    else:
        # Generic token to exercise parser paths
        s = _random_ascii(r, 1, 24)

    # Occasionally prepend a vendor/OS prefix pattern that includes a dot already
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        pref = r.choice(VENDOR_PREFIXES)
        if not s.startswith(pref):
            s = pref + s

    # Ensure length cap
    if len(s) > MAX_LEN:
        s = s[:MAX_LEN]

    # Avoid empty string
    if not s:
        s = 'C'

    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Create a small pool and pick one to add variety while deterministic per seed
    candidates = [_make_candidate(r) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 5))]
    s = r.choice(candidates)
    # Return UTF-8 bytes; fuzzer will pass as C string (no explicit NUL needed)
    return s.encode('utf-8')

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for raw byte buffers tailored to libusb transfer/descriptors use.
# We focus on producing plausible USB descriptor blobs and control transfer payloads
# that are valid according to USB spec, while remaining small (<=64 bytes typical here).

# Utilities

def _le16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', x & 0xFFFF)


def _le32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


# Descriptor builders

def build_device_descriptor(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # USB device descriptor (18 bytes)
    bLength = 18
    bDescriptorType = 0x01  # LIBUSB_DT_DEVICE
    bcdUSB = r.choice([0x0110, 0x0200, 0x0210, 0x0300])
    bDeviceClass = r.choice([0x00, 0x02, 0x03, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0E, 0xEF, 0xFF])
    bDeviceSubClass = r.randrange(0, 256)
    bDeviceProtocol = r.randrange(0, 256)
    bMaxPacketSize0 = r.choice([8, 16, 32, 64])
    idVendor = r.randrange(0, 0x10000)
    idProduct = r.randrange(0, 0x10000)
    bcdDevice = r.randrange(0, 0x10000)
    iManufacturer = r.randrange(0, 4)
    iProduct = r.randrange(0, 4)
    iSerialNumber = r.randrange(0, 4)
    bNumConfigurations = r.choice([1, 2])
    return bytes([
        bLength,
        bDescriptorType,
    ]) + _le16(bcdUSB) + bytes([
        bDeviceClass,
        bDeviceSubClass,
        bDeviceProtocol,
        bMaxPacketSize0,
    ]) + _le16(idVendor) + _le16(idProduct) + _le16(bcdDevice) + bytes([
        iManufacturer,
        iProduct,
        iSerialNumber,
        bNumConfigurations,
    ])


def build_config_descriptor_block(r: random.Random, total_len_limit: int = 64) -> bytes:
    # Build a configuration descriptor followed by one interface and one endpoint
    # Keep total <= total_len_limit
    # Configuration descriptor: 9 bytes
    cfg_bLength = 9
    cfg_bDescriptorType = 0x02
    # Interface and endpoint lengths we'll compute

    # Interface descriptor: 9 bytes
    if_bLength = 9
    if_bDescriptorType = 0x04
    bInterfaceNumber = 0
    bAlternateSetting = 0
    bNumEndpoints = 1
    bInterfaceClass = r.choice([0x02, 0x03, 0x08, 0x0A, 0x0E, 0xFF])
    bInterfaceSubClass = r.randrange(0, 256)
    bInterfaceProtocol = r.randrange(0, 256)
    iInterface = 0

    # Endpoint descriptor: 7 bytes
    ep_bLength = 7
    ep_bDescriptorType = 0x05
    # Address: bits 0..3 ep num 1..15, bit7 direction
    ep_num = r.randint(1, 15)
    ep_dir_in = r.choice([0, 1])
    bEndpointAddress = ep_num | (0x80 if ep_dir_in else 0x00)
    # bmAttributes: choose bulk/interrupt/isoch
    xfer_type = r.choice([1, 2, 3])  # 1 isoch, 2 bulk, 3 intr
    bmAttributes = xfer_type & 0x3
    # wMaxPacketSize: pick typical sizes
    if xfer_type == 2:  # bulk
        wMaxPacketSize = r.choice([64, 512, 1024])
    elif xfer_type == 3:  # interrupt
        wMaxPacketSize = r.choice([8, 16, 32, 64, 256])
    else:  # isochronous
        wMaxPacketSize = r.choice([1024, 512, 256])
    bInterval = r.choice([1, 2, 4, 8, 16]) if xfer_type != 2 else 0

    ep_desc = bytes([
        ep_bLength,
        ep_bDescriptorType,
        bEndpointAddress,
        bmAttributes,
    ]) + _le16(wMaxPacketSize) + bytes([bInterval])

    if_desc = bytes([
        if_bLength,
        if_bDescriptorType,
        bInterfaceNumber,
        bAlternateSetting,
        bNumEndpoints,
        bInterfaceClass,
        bInterfaceSubClass,
        bInterfaceProtocol,
        iInterface,
    ])

    # Compute wTotalLength
    extra = b""
    total = cfg_bLength + len(if_desc) + len(ep_desc) + len(extra)
    wTotalLength = total
    if wTotalLength > total_len_limit:
        # Trim: drop extra (already empty), ensure under limit by reducing nothing else
        wTotalLength = min(wTotalLength, total_len_limit)

    cfg_desc = bytes([
        cfg_bLength,
        cfg_bDescriptorType,
    ]) + _le16(wTotalLength) + bytes([
        1,   # bNumInterfaces
        1,   # bConfigurationValue
        0,   # iConfiguration
        0x80 | (r.choice([0, 0x20])),  # bmAttributes: bus powered, maybe remote wakeup
        r.choice([0, 50, 100, 250]),   # MaxPower in 2mA units
    ])

    blob = cfg_desc + if_desc + ep_desc + extra
    # Ensure wTotalLength matches actual
    blob = blob[:2] + _le16(len(blob)) + blob[4:]
    return blob


def build_string_descriptor_ascii(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # The fuzzer uses ASCII getter which returns UTF-8 bytes into buffer.
    # Provide readable ASCII/UTF-8 bytes up to max_len.
    length = r.randint(0, max_len)
    if length == 0:
        return b""
    alphabet = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 -_/."
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    return s.encode('utf-8')


def build_string_descriptor_utf16le(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Raw GET_STRING_DESCRIPTOR returns UTF-16LE payload; we'll craft a plausible one.
    # USB string descriptor: bLength, bDescriptorType=0x03, UTF-16LE chars.
    text_len = max(0, min((max_len - 2) // 2, r.randint(0, 20)))
    text_chars = "USB Fuzz Device Manufacturer Product Serial"
    s = ''.join(r.choice(text_chars) for _ in range(text_len))
    payload = s.encode('utf-16le')
    bLength = 2 + len(payload)
    return bytes([bLength, 0x03]) + payload


def build_control_data_stage(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Provide small, sensible data for control transfers. Could be descriptor-like or vendor data.
    choice = r.randrange(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        # Short vendor data
        n = r.randint(0, max_len)
        return r.randbytes(n)
    elif choice == 1:
        # Little-endian ushort array
        count = max_len // 2
        arr = [r.randrange(0, 0x10000) for _ in range(r.randint(0, count))]
        return b"".join(_le16(v) for v in arr)
    elif choice == 2 and max_len >= 18:
        return build_device_descriptor(r)[:max_len]
    else:
        # Small config descriptor block
        return build_config_descriptor_block(r, total_len_limit=max_len)


def build_descriptor_blob(r: random.Random, kind: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # kind maps to desc_type selection used by fuzzer helper
    if kind == 0x01:  # device
        blob = build_device_descriptor(r)
    elif kind == 0x02:  # config
        blob = build_config_descriptor_block(r, total_len_limit=max_len)
    elif kind == 0x03:  # string (raw UTF-16LE)
        blob = build_string_descriptor_utf16le(r, max_len)
    elif kind == 0x04:  # interface
        # Minimal interface descriptor
        b = bytes([
            9, 0x04, 0, 0, 1,
            r.choice([0x02, 0x03, 0x08, 0x0A, 0x0E, 0xFF]),
            r.randrange(0, 256),
            r.randrange(0, 256),
            0,
        ])
        blob = b
    elif kind == 0x05:  # endpoint
        # Minimal endpoint descriptor
        ep_num = r.randint(1, 15)
        dir_in = r.choice([0, 1])
        xfer_type = r.choice([1, 2, 3])
        wMax = r.choice([64, 512, 1024])
        bInterval = r.choice([0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16])
        b = bytes([
            7, 0x05, ep_num | (0x80 if dir_in else 0x00), xfer_type & 0x3,
        ]) + _le16(wMax) + bytes([bInterval])
        blob = b
    else:
        blob = r.randbytes(r.randint(0, max_len))
    return blob[:max_len]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide which target stub to favor to craft appropriate buffer sizes/content.
    target = r.choice([
        'control_transfer',
        'bulk_transfer',
        'interrupt_transfer',
        'get_descriptor',
        'get_string_descriptor',
        'get_string_descriptor_ascii',
        'device_string',
    ])

    # The fuzz harness uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to fill payload buffers of sizes:
    # - control: up to 32 bytes
    # - bulk: up to 32 bytes
    # - interrupt: up to 16 bytes
    # - get_descriptor/string helpers: up to 64 bytes
    # We'll return a buffer with mixed concatenated chunks; the fuzzer can slice from it.

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Always prepend a plausible descriptor so reads at small lengths are meaningful
    if target in ('get_descriptor', 'get_string_descriptor'):
        # Choose a desc type consistent with helper choices
        desc_type = r.choice([0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05])
        chunks.append(build_descriptor_blob(r, desc_type, max_len=64))
    elif target == 'get_string_descriptor_ascii':
        chunks.append(build_string_descriptor_ascii(r, max_len=64))
    elif target == 'device_string':
        # Provide readable UTF-8 bytes (converted from device string helper expects UTF-8 buffer)
        chunks.append(build_string_descriptor_ascii(r, max_len=256))
    elif target == 'control_transfer':
        chunks.append(build_control_data_stage(r, max_len=32))
    elif target == 'bulk_transfer':
        # Arbitrary payload; choose printable to be benign
        chunks.append(build_string_descriptor_ascii(r, max_len=32))
    elif target == 'interrupt_transfer':
        chunks.append(build_string_descriptor_ascii(r, max_len=16))

    # Add a secondary chunk to increase variety for subsequent FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls
    chunks.append(build_config_descriptor_block(r, total_len_limit=64))
    chunks.append(build_device_descriptor(r))

    # Optionally append random bytes (small) to cover vendor data
    chunks.append(r.randbytes(r.randint(0, 16)))

    blob = b"".join(chunks)
    # Ensure size <= 4096 (it will be small anyway); trim if necessary
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
    return blob
